channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 42nd Annual International Exhibition · University of Texas at Tyler
item.description: The Department of Art and Art History at The University of Texas at Tyler runs one of the longest-running juried competitions in the region, now in its 42nd year, shown at the university's Meadows Gallery. The 2027 edition is juried by Diana Roberts, an arts writer, curator and arts administrator in San Antonio who has been Director of The Center for Spirituality and the Arts, Curator of the Airport Art Spaces at San Antonio International Airport, and Gallery Director for Galeria Ortiz Contemporary. The call is explicitly open to two-dimensional media, and photographs are named alongside paintings, drawings, prints and fiber art; work must have been made in the last three years. Awards take the form of purchase awards: the department buys three to six works from the exhibition each year and adds them to its permanent collection, much of which hangs across the UT Tyler campus as a teaching resource. Entry is $35 for up to three works, judged from digital files; the CaFE entry window opens on 24 August 2026. Framed works must use Plexiglass rather than glass and weigh under 50 pounds; artists cover shipping both ways and must include a pre-paid return label. Notification is 14 December 2026, work is due at the gallery by 8 January 2027, and the exhibition runs 19 January to 5 March 2027 with a reception and juror's presentation on 4 March. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Purchase awards (cash).

item.title: Solastalgia — 16th Annual International Juried Exhibition · A.D. Gallery, University of North Carolina at Pembroke
item.description: The A.D. Gallery at UNC Pembroke builds its 16th annual international juried exhibition around solastalgia — the term coined by philosopher Glenn Albrecht for the distress caused by environmental change experienced while still living in the place that is changing. The gallery describes it as "a form of homesickness felt without ever leaving home: the grief of watching a familiar landscape change around you — receding shorelines, vanishing species, drought-cracked earth, wildfire smoke over childhood streets, development replacing the sounds of nature." Interpretations may be personal, political, poetic, documentary, speculative or abstract, and suggested threads include loss of place-identity to climate change or extraction, memory and landscape as before/after, solastalgia as distinct from nostalgia, collective environmental grief, and Indigenous and generational knowledge of land in flux. Two-dimensional and three-dimensional works, installations and digital media including video up to five minutes are all eligible. Juror Carla Rokes is an artist and educator originally from the Carolinas with a BFA from UNC Charlotte and an MFA from Pratt Institute. Prizes are $400, $200 and $100. Entry is $35 for up to three works, with an artist statement on how the work engages the theme and a one-page CV required. AI-generated work will not be considered, and work must be original and made in the last three years. Notification is 15 December 2026, accepted work must reach Pembroke, North Carolina between 19 and 22 January 2027, and the exhibition runs 11 February to 3 March 2027. This is a non-profit gallery supported by the university, so work is not for sale during the show. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $400 first prize + $200 second + $100 third.

item.title: 1st Annual National Juried Exhibition · Visual Arts Gallery, Governors State University
item.description: The Visual Arts Gallery at Governors State University, south of Chicago, launches its first National Juried Exhibition and invites artists living anywhere in the United States to submit contemporary work. The gallery — which sits alongside the Nathan Manilow Sculpture Park and has run a national juried programme since 2010 — says it is looking for work that reflects innovation, technical excellence and compelling ideas across a broad range of media, and encourages artists at every career stage. Guest juror Kimberly Oliva is a Chicago-based Midwest curator and the owner of Oliva Gallery, where she has curated more than 175 interdisciplinary exhibitions; her curatorial work has been shown at SOFA Chicago, Door County Contemporary and art and design fairs across Texas, and she founded the Mozart Park Mural Program. She will select works on artistic merit, conceptual strength and craftsmanship. Entry is $35 for up to three original works made in the past three years, submitted with an artist statement and full details for each piece. Work previously shown at the gallery is not eligible; Governors State alumni are welcome to apply. The exhibition is on view 7–18 December 2026 and 4–22 January 2027, with a closure across the university holiday break. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: The Art of Health Services · Nicolet College
item.description: A free open call from The Gallery at Nicolet College in Rhinelander, Wisconsin, part of the college's ongoing "The Art of" exhibition series. The Art of Health Services asks for artwork inspired by healing, resilience, caregiving and the impact healthcare workers have on individuals, families and communities, and is mounted in recognition of the college's Nursing, Medical Assistant, Phlebotomy, Radiography, Substance Use Disorder Counseling and Human Services programmes. The call names no medium restriction and asks for work "through a variety of artistic media" that explores the experiences, connections and dedication that define careers in health services. There is no entry fee and no commission on sales — if a piece sells, the college passes the enquiry to the artist and the two settle it directly. Artists may submit up to three pieces. Entries are reviewed by Nicolet's Team Art committee together with health and human services faculty, with acceptances going out the week of 19 October. Hand deliveries are taken on 20 November and shipped work must arrive by 25 November with return paperwork and pre-paid postage included; the opening reception is 9 December and the show closes 23 January 2027. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Artspace Open Call for Proposals
item.description: Artspace, a 501(c)(3) artist-run nonprofit gallery in Richmond, Virginia, opens its annual call for exhibition proposals for the 2027 season. The Exhibition Committee reviews proposals for shows in all genres, and proposals may be for individual, group or joint exhibitions, or for curating the work of others. Four slots are available in 2027: 26 March–17 April, 23 April–22 May, 27 August–18 September and 24 September–16 October. Selection criteria are published in full and cover artistic merit and track record, how the exhibition contributes to Artspace's mission of building stronger communities through contemporary arts, how it fosters opportunities to gather with and learn from artists, how it coordinates with other shows in the same period, and how it broadens awareness of contemporary art in and around Greater Richmond. Applicants submit an art resume or CV, a written proposal, preferred dates, any planned programming or workshops, and five to ten image, video or sound files. The proposal fee is $35 and goes to operations and programming, but the committee will waive it — email them before submitting if the fee is a hardship. Work should have been made within five years of the exhibition date unless the proposal is a retrospective, and everything must fit through a door 33 inches wide by 82¾ inches high. Full-time students are not eligible to apply for individual or joint shows. Selected exhibitors are notified by 13 November 2026 and the full slate is announced by the end of December. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $35 (waiver available on request). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Roadblocks · Studio Montclair
item.description: Studio Montclair, a nationwide nonprofit of exhibiting artists based in Montclair, New Jersey, invites work for Roadblocks, an exhibition about barriers both tangible and abstract. The gallery writes that roadblocks "come in many forms — physical, cultural, societal and psychological" and that these barriers often hinder connection, understanding and progress; artists are asked to examine how such roadblocks are constructed, perceived and sometimes dismantled. All mediums are accepted, including video and installation. The jurors are Debbie Silberberg, MPA, an assemblage and fibre artist, guest curator at the Rockefeller Gallery and a member of the Rockland County Art in Public Places Committee, and Lisa D'Amico, PhD, a painter and mixed-media artist, head curator at the Rockefeller Gallery, a member of the same committee and an advisory board member of the Hopper House Museum. The show hangs in Studio Montclair's Leach Gallery at 641 Bloomfield Avenue. Entry is free for Studio Montclair members and $42 for non-members, for a maximum of three works. Work must have been completed within the past five years, must not have been shown in any previous Studio Montclair exhibition, and giclée reproductions of original art are not accepted. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free for members; $42 non-members. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Relative Impulse · Joseph Gross Gallery, University of Arizona
item.description: A free open call from the Joseph Gross Gallery, the 2,000-square-foot contemporary space inside the University of Arizona School of Art in Tucson, next door to the University of Arizona Museum of Art. Relative Impulse features artworks for which the making — or destroying — of family archives is material and metaphor: "Funny, heart-wrenching, or bizarre, using the ephemera of memory itself or a copy of a copy, each artwork reminds us that everything's relative." Artists of any career stage and any media or material process are eligible, and work made at any time qualifies; up to three artworks may be submitted, each on its own form with two to four images, and there are no size restrictions. Curated by gallery director lydia see, with jurying, preparation, installation and marketing handled by the School of Art's Gallery Praxis class and its student gallery managers. There is no entry fee, but selected artists ship or hand-deliver their own work and provide a return shipping label — the gallery says shipping assistance may be available to artists for whom the cost would be a barrier to exhibiting. Notifications go out 8 September, work must arrive by 29 September, the exhibition runs 13 October 2026 to 28 January 2027 with a reception on 22 October, and packages are mailed back by 10 February 2027. Current University of Arizona students, staff and faculty may also submit. No living or organic matter may be exhibited, and selected works cannot be withdrawn before the exhibition closes. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Misfits & Mayhem · Denison Arts Council
item.description: The Denison Arts Council closes its exhibition year at 517 Gallery in the downtown Denison Cultural Arts District in north Texas with the one show on its calendar that has no theme at all. Misfits & Mayhem opens the doors to “the artists and artworks which didn’t quite mesh with the themes of our previous shows” — the council writes that any size, medium, subject matter and style is welcome, and pitches it as a chance for emerging artists to test the waters and for established artists to show something they haven’t previously had the chance to show. Applications are made through a Google Form linked from the call page, which states plainly: “There is no fee for submission or participation in the exhibition.” The gallery keeps a 20% commission on work sold. Artists may enter 2-D wall pieces or prints, with limited shelf and pedestal space for 3-D work, plus small low-priced pieces for the gallery boutique. Work must arrive wired and ready to hang — sawtooth hangers are not accepted, though staff will wire a piece for $10 — and must be the artist’s own original or a reproduction of their own work; AI-generated images are not eligible. Selected artists complete a W-9. The gallery committee responds on 16 October, work is dropped off on 8 November, and the exhibition opens with a reception on 14 November from 4 to 6 pm, has a midway reception on 12 December, and closes on 3 January 2027 when artists collect their work. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Analog: An Antidote to AI Art · New Bedford Art Museum
item.description: Juried exhibition at the New Bedford Art Museum celebrating what algorithms cannot replicate: intuition, vulnerability, touch, chance, personal history, and the decisions embedded in the creative process. Rather than rejecting technology, the show asks what makes art unmistakably human, seeking work that reveals touch, struggle and experimentation. Open to all visual art media and genres including photography, with work created wholly or partially through generative AI expressly ineligible. Juried by Roddy Schrock, sound artist and former director of Eyebeam, New York's center for art and technology. Exhibition December 10, 2026 - March 21, 2027, with an opening reception December 10. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: $40 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 first + $500 second.

item.title: LENS 2027 · Perspective Gallery
item.description: 17th annual juried international exhibition of fine art photography at Perspective Gallery, a not-for-profit photography cooperative in Evanston, Illinois. All subject matter and photographic processes are welcome except AI, and the call is open to photographers nationally and internationally. Juried by Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director and Curator of the Houston Center for Photography and previously Dean and Managing Director of Education at the International Center of Photography in New York. Work must have been created within the past five years; work previously shown at Perspective Gallery is ineligible. Exhibition March 4-28, 2027, with an opening reception and awards March 6 and a virtual artists' talk March 11. Artists receive 60% of the sale price of any work sold. The entry window opens 23 September 2026 — the gallery's prospectus states the date only inside its fee line ("Early Bird Submission ($35) opens on September 23"), and the portal is closed to entrants until then. — Deadline: January 6, 2027. Fee: $40 (5 images); $35 early bird to Oct 31. Prize: $300 Juror's Award + $200 + $150.

item.title: Hale Master of Fine Art Residency 2027 · Artists Association of Nantucket
item.description: The Artists Association of Nantucket's fully funded Hale Residency is a month-long stay on Nantucket for artists who are currently enrolled in an MFA programme or who graduated from one within the past five years. The residency is described by AAN as designed for an artist “whose work explores aesthetic beauty”, and it exists to give that artist uninterrupted time: there is no expectation to teach, exhibit or present work, though exhibition and community engagement are encouraged. Hale residencies run only in January, February and March. The selected artist receives $500 toward travel and a $2,000 stipend for materials and living expenses, and stays in the Kaaren and Charles Hale apartment for Artists in Residence — a furnished studio apartment inside AAN's Visual Arts Center on Amelia Drive — with a private studio equipped with tables, easels, rolling carts and a large sink. AAN's printmaking and ceramics studios are also available to residents around the regular class schedule. Applications go by email as a single PDF and ask for a CV of up to three pages, a 200-word artist statement, a 200-word bio, 12 digital images with an image list, a 300-word cover letter and contacts for three references. The deadline is 31 August 2026 and announcements are made by 21 September 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 + Residency.

item.title: Environmental Artist Residency 2027 · Artists Association of Nantucket
item.description: A funded residency on Nantucket for artists whose practice engages the environment, climate and the natural world, hosted by the Artists Association of Nantucket and supported by the GHYC Foundation. The island is the point: a coastal place undergoing rapid erosion, sea-level rise and habitat change, and the residency asks the selected artist to make new work informed by that landscape and to put it into public conversation. The 2027 edition runs 11 April to 8 May. The award is a $3,000 artist stipend, $500 in travel expenses, three weeks of housing in AAN's Kaaren and Charles Hale apartment at the Visual Arts Center, a private studio, and an exhibition in AAN's Champion Gallery — which may show work made during the residency, existing work, or both. In return the artist gives an artist talk, develops one community creative experience such as a workshop or participatory artwork, and takes part in public engagement including work with local youth; an optional strand invites collaboration with the Linda Loring Nature Foundation, the Nantucket Conservation Foundation or the Maria Mitchell Association on a walk-and-talk or site-based project. Eligibility is open to emerging and established artists aged 18 or over, and AAN states that artists in all mediums are welcome. Applications are a single PDF sent by email, with 8–12 images or links to time-based work, a CV, a 300–500 word statement and a 500–750 word residency proposal. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 + Residency + Exhibition.

item.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Best Portfolio 2027
item.description: Blank Wall Gallery's annual international portfolio contest, run to find and promote a single photographer rather than a single strong image. The winner receives a two-week solo exhibition at the gallery's new premises in Athens, with Blank Wall producing and financing up to 40 prints (40x50cm and 50x70cm) in its own labs at no cost to the artist, and covering everything else needed to stage the show even if the photographer cannot attend. The gallery sends newsletter invitations to its full contact list, issues a personalised press release to magazines, presents the exhibition on its website alongside its other solo shows, and afterwards compiles a detailed folder of publications, installation photographs, posters and other material and sends it to the artist. The winner also receives a certificate of achievement and a free entry to the following year's competition. Two further portfolios receive certificates of honourable mention and the right to submit ten photographs to one of Blank Wall's group contests, and every entrant gets a 25% discount on prints made at the gallery lab through the end of 2027. Entry is open to amateurs and professionals over 18; each artist may submit up to three portfolios of 10 to 20 photographs each. Submission is by email, WeTransfer or Dropbox after paying the fee. — Deadline: May 31, 2027. Fee: €50 per portfolio. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Rotterdam Photo 2027 — Projects
item.description: The international projects strand of Rotterdam Photo's open call for its 2027 edition, which runs 17–21 March 2027 during Rotterdam Art Week. The theme is 'VIBRANCE – The Pulse of a Living World', an exploration of energy in its many forms, from the intimate to the collective and from physical presence to digital intensity; the festival asks photographers to read vibrance freely as a social condition, emotional state, visual rhythm or conceptual framework. Selected photographers each receive a dedicated exhibition space inside the festival's container village in the centre of Rotterdam, where the work becomes part of a large-scale public exhibition seen by more than 10,000 visitors. Artists keep curatorial freedom over their own space, may sell work during the festival, and Rotterdam Photo takes no commission on sales. Participants also join the Rotterdam Photo Talks and networking programme, appear in the official festival programme and publications, and are promoted through festival and partner platforms including LensCulture, Dodho Magazine and All About Photo. The category is open worldwide to emerging and established practitioners working across documentary, conceptual, experimental and interdisciplinary image-based practice; entrants must be at least 16. Submissions are reviewed over three rounds by a named selection committee and judged on artistic strength and originality, conceptual depth and relevance to the theme. Photographers may apply to more than one category, with each submission reviewed separately. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: €29 per entry until September 7, 2026, then €35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rotterdam Photo 2027 — Single Image
item.description: The single-image strand of Rotterdam Photo's open call for its 2027 edition, held 17–21 March 2027 during Rotterdam Art Week under the theme 'VIBRANCE – The Pulse of a Living World'. Rather than a screen or a print in a booth, each selected image is turned into a large-scale public installation: a PVC print measuring 2.5 by 2.5 metres, mounted on the exterior of the festival's shipping containers and displayed in public space for the whole festival period, with production covered in full by the festival. Selected photographers are featured across festival and partner channels including LensCulture, Dodho Magazine and All About Photo, are published in and included in the festival programme, can take part in the Rotterdam Photo Talks and networking events, and reach an audience of more than 10,000 visitors in central Rotterdam. The category is open worldwide to professional and amateur photographers and image-makers working across photography and visual media; entrants must be at least 16 as of the date of entry. A professional selection committee assesses images over three rounds on visual strength, conceptual clarity, emotional and spatial impact, and relevance to the theme. Photographers may enter more than one category of the open call, and each submission is reviewed separately. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: €19 per image. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rotterdam Photo 2027 — Dutch Talent Project Grant
item.description: A production grant for emerging photographers based in or trained in the Netherlands, run by Rotterdam Photo with Amarte Fonds as part of the festival's 2027 open call. Five selected artists each receive €3,000 to develop new work responding to the festival theme 'VIBRANCE – The Pulse of a Living World', together with curatorial guidance and artistic coaching throughout the development process. The resulting work is shown as a work-in-progress exhibition at Rotterdam Photo 2027, held 17–21 March 2027 during Rotterdam Art Week, with a dedicated exhibition space and inclusion in the group exhibition and the official festival programme. Grantees also take part in the Rotterdam Photo Talks and networking events, are documented in 'Rotterdam Snapshots' video portraits of the artistic process shared on YouTube and social media, and are put in front of curators, press and international photography professionals. The festival additionally names onward exhibition opportunities in Barcelona with the International Photo Festival Association, at the Backlight festival in Tampere, at the Tbilisi Art Fair, and at Photo Schweiz through Directors' Choice. Eligibility is open to photographers based in the Netherlands, currently studying there, or who completed studies there, specifically third- and fourth-year art academy students, alumni of photography or related visual arts programmes since 2020, and self-taught photographers with up to five years of practical experience. Projects begun during study qualify if they are extended or deepened beyond the academic context. Entry is free. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Members Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts brings its annual Members Show back in person for a second year. The top fifty selected works go up on the gallery's Community Walls in Portland, with a broader selection of submitted work shown on the Blue Sky website. There is no theme: the gallery asks only for your best work. Any Blue Sky member in current good standing may submit up to three high-resolution images, one submission per artist, with an optional artist statement of up to 100 words about your practice. Membership is not a closed gate — the call page links straight to Blue Sky's join page, and the $50 Champion tier lists eligibility to submit to the Annual Members Exhibition among its benefits, so any photographer can become eligible by joining. The exhibition opens Thursday, October 1 at 5 PM. Blue Sky is a non-profit founded in 1975 by a group of five young photographers as the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, now in its fiftieth-anniversary year, and the Members Show is the point in its calendar where the membership itself gets the walls. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free (Blue Sky membership from $50/year required). Prize: Exhibition on Blue Sky's Community Walls.

item.title: A Latin America & Caribbean Exhibition · Stamford Art Association
item.description: The Stamford Art Association's second annual Latin America and Caribbean show, presented at the Townhouse Gallery in Stamford and online on the SAA website. The theme is open to all media and all interpretations, and the association is explicit that you do not need to be of Latin American or Caribbean descent to enter: submissions are open to anyone whose work engages with or is inspired by these regions and themes. Up to nine works may be submitted. The returning juror is Valeria Ochoa, SAA's gallery manager and board secretary, a literature and language educator with an MA in linguistics and an MA in curriculum and instruction who works in Norwalk Public Schools; a first-generation Colombian, she writes and photographs around ancestry, roots and lineage and their ties to land and belonging. Work must be original and not previously shown at the SAA gallery, no larger than 48 by 60 inches framed, wired for hanging and hand delivered — there is no shipping option, with receiving on September 18 and 19 and pickup on October 23 and 24. Photographs are exempt from the rule requiring prints to be signed and numbered as a limited edition; giclees are not accepted. The gallery takes 30 percent commission on work sold. The show runs September 24 to October 22, 2026, opening Thursday September 24, 5:30 to 7 PM. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $35 + $15 each addl ($30/$10 members). Prize: None listed.

item.title: BBA Artist Prize 2027
item.description: BBA Gallery's flagship all-media prize, running since 2018 and open to anyone eighteen or over working in any medium, photography included. There is no theme and no restriction on training, nationality or career stage; the only structural bar is that entrants must not be under an exclusive gallery contract, and that artists already represented by BBA are ineligible. Entrants submit up to five works with a statement of no more than 300 words and a CV. A jury of industry professionals selects a longlist of fifty artists, who are promoted by the gallery and receive a certificate of nomination, and from those fifty a shortlist of twenty who exhibit at BBA Gallery in Berlin. First prize is €1,000 with a solo exhibition at BBA Gallery, an Artsy profile and press, newsletter and social promotion; second is €700, third €500, and an Audience Award carries €300, each with an Artsy profile and promotion. Past first-prize winners include Chung-Kun Wang of Taiwan, Dominik Adamec of the Czech Republic and László Máthé of Romania. Entry is through the BBA Prizes platform, where earlybird access is already open and work can be uploaded at any point before the deadline. — Deadline: December 7, 2027. Fee: €39 (up to 5 works). Prize: €1,000 + solo exhibition at BBA Gallery (2nd €700, 3rd €500, Audience Award €300).

item.title: Recent Work v1 · Limner Gallery
item.description: SlowArt Productions and the Limner Gallery in Hudson, New York open their next thematic group exhibition to artists working in any media and any style, from the abstract to the figurative. The premise is simply newness: the show asks for an artist's most recent work, and eligibility is drawn as a date rather than a subject, with any piece completed after January 1, 2025 accepted. Photography, digital work, graphics, painting, drawing and sculpture are all named as eligible media, and video may be entered by supplying a link to a hosted file, each link counting as one image. Wall-mounted work must be no taller than 72 inches and no wider than 120 inches; sculpture must fit through a 36-inch door. Selected artists are shown in the gallery from March 4 to April 3, 2027, and the exhibition is also carried on the Limner Gallery website and promoted through the gallery's social channels. Work may be offered for sale or not for sale at the artist's own price, with the gallery taking a 35 percent commission on sales. Entry is by email with JPG attachments of about 2500 pixels on the longest side, or a link to a personal image page. Artists accepted to exhibit are charged no further exhibition or promotional fees. Results are posted publicly at slowart.com/results on or before December 31, 2026, which the gallery states is the official notification rather than the email that accompanies it. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 4 works), $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art & Noise · Women's Caucus for Art of Greater Washington, DC
item.description: The Washington, DC chapter of the Women's Caucus for Art invites women and non-binary artists based in DC, Maryland or Virginia to make work about how sound and silence shape a creative life. The premise is the music blasting in a studio, the ambient hush of a museum, the rhythm and harmony artists reach for without words. Photography is named among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, fiber work, mixed media and free-standing sculpture; commercially produced prints, giclees, jewellery and performance are not accepted, and video or film needing an external power source is considered case by case. Work is juried by LaPrea Rich, an abstract expressionist from Prince George's County, Maryland who has shown in more than twenty juried exhibitions since 2023 and is a member of the Arlington Artists Alliance, the Maryland Federation of Art and the McLean Art Society. Selected work hangs at the Harmony Hall Arts Center in Fort Washington, Maryland from November 30, 2026 to January 9, 2027, with an artist reception on December 5. Two-dimensional work must be no larger than 72 inches in any direction including its frame and must arrive exhibition-ready with wire and D-rings; sawtooth hangers are refused. Harmony Hall takes 25 percent of any sale and WCADC takes no commission. The chapter is entirely volunteer-run and directs entry fees to its Visual Arts Scholarship and to artist relief. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (1-3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Raw Blood and Nerve — Artist Showcase · Dickinson Publishing Group
item.description: Dickinson Publishing Group is a small horror fiction imprint working out of Brooklyn, New York. It is launching a magazine called Raw Blood and Nerve that will carry short fiction alongside one section per issue given over entirely to a single artist's work, and this open call is for that section. The magazine prints in black and white, so the editor asks for work that is either monochrome already or that the artist is comfortable seeing reproduced without colour. The register wanted is dark, surreal and macabre: the reference points offered are Odilon Redon and Gustave Dore on one side and H.R. Giger and Junji Ito on the other, with the editor cheerfully admitting to being a layman about art-historical precision. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside painting, sketch and graphite drawing. Between five and twelve pieces may be submitted, one entry per artist, and there is no fee. The selected artist receives a per diem of fifty to one hundred dollars depending on how many pieces are taken, which the imprint frames plainly as the most a very small publisher can offer; against that it notes that its new releases typically sell over four thousand ebooks and that two of its titles have passed ten thousand units, so the work will reach readers. Work made with AI is refused outright, and the imprint states that an AI submission will cost the artist consideration of any future submission as well. — Deadline: September 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $50-$100 + publication.

item.title: Rawhead & Bloody Bones — Halloween Special Issue
item.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of poetry, fiction, nonfiction and visual art, named after one of the folkloric bogeymen once used to frighten children into obedience. It is not a horror publication, but it is interested in work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft and surprising clarity, and it reads the arts as a form of resistance. In folklore Rawhead is half of a monstrous duo, Rawhead & Bloody Bones, and every year in time for Halloween the journal teams up with the other half of its namesake for a special issue celebrating that myth. Submissions for Bloody Bones are open from August 15th to October 1st. The editors are seeking work that explores shadowed corners of being — ghosts, folklore, grief, hunger, rage, queerness, transformation — with monsters as metaphor or as real as the artist needs them to be. Poetry, prose, hybrid work and visual art are all welcome, and submission standards are the same as for regular issues: the visual art category takes three to ten pieces in any medium, explicitly including photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture, uploaded as high-quality images of at least 1500px. The art editor's standing brief is work that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty rather than horror or gore, citing Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Submission is free and the journal states it is committed to always offering free submissions to all writers and artists, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that have no bearing on editorial decisions. Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and previously published work is welcome where rights have reverted and at least six months have passed. AI-generated content is not accepted. Rawhead actively seeks submissions from creators of all backgrounds and lived experiences, naming BIPOC, Indigenous, refugee and diaspora, LGBTQIA2S+, disabled, neurodivergent, incarcerated and economically precarious creators among others. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $100 + Publication.

item.title: Flanelle Print No. 48 — October 2026
item.description: Flanelle is a Montreal-based fashion, arts and culture magazine founded in 2012, known for raw editorials, a heavily image-led approach and a coffee-table production standard on quality paper. It publishes quarterly — January, April, July and October — in both print-on-demand and digital editions, distributed internationally, and its pages are built from editorial contributions by independent photographers. Print No. 48 publishes in October 2026 and is open to photographers, artists and designers worldwide. Each photo set should include a minimum of ten photographs following the issue's theme and mood board, and editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle; for fashion and beauty editorials the magazine asks for at least three looks and six photographs, with full team and wardrobe credits entered at submission. Review runs in two phases: an initial decision on submission, then a second round about a week before the deadline, so the magazine advises submitting closer to the deadline rather than early. Standard print submission is free. Optional paid upgrades exist for cover placement, advertorials and priority publishing, and the magazine charges a $20 revision fee for credit corrections after submission and a $100 fee to withdraw a series once it has been accepted into print. Selected work appears in the quarterly print issue and digital edition, with possible exposure across the magazine's social channels; published teams receive a free digital version on request. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: States — Open Call 2026 · Belarusian Association of Photographers
item.description: The Belarusian Association of Photographers (BAP) invites photographers to its open call «States», framed by the organisers as "more than the emotions of one person — a frame, a canvas, a boundary and a portal at once". The call asks photographers to stop and consider how the world is refracted inside a person through what they live through, both literal and metaphorical, and to look at those inner worlds without black and white — in all their shades, colours, reflections and registers of perception. What interests the organisers is not only what a person feels but what brings them into that state, how it alters their perception of the world around them, and how that world is itself able to immerse a person in particular states. No genre, style or manner of interpreting the theme is prescribed: documentary story, portrait, autobiographical statement, observation of an environment, conceptual series or a visual investigation of a social phenomenon are all welcome, provided the work carries the author's own vision of a state and its connection to person and world. Entries go into one of two categories — Solo, a single self-standing image, or Series, four to ten photographs held together by one idea, theme or visual concept and read as a single statement. Work must have been made no earlier than 2024, files are JPEG at a minimum 4000 px on the long side and up to 5 MB, and a description of up to 300 words covering a short biography, the title, the work itself and its relation to the theme must accompany the application. Works created entirely with generative neural networks are not accepted. Entry is free and one person may submit a single application in one category. Selected authors become participants in the project's final exhibition, which opens on 26 September 2026 in Zhodishki, Belarus. Applications are sent by email with «Состояния» in the subject line; finalists are announced on 12 September 2026. — Deadline: September 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: BEERS London 40-Day Residency
item.description: BEERS London runs a rolling, year-round 40-Day Residency for artists working in any medium, based in the UK or internationally, who are able to come to London. For forty days a selected artist receives studio and work space, an honorarium towards lodging, flight and materials, curatorial and professional development support, and the freedom to shape their own working schedule; the programme is designed to balance focused studio time with studio visits, professional development and optional public engagement, and concludes with a public presentation or exhibition of the work developed during the residency. Selected artists also receive professional documentation of finished works and promotion through the gallery's mailing list and social channels. Between two and four residency sessions are held each year and there is no application deadline: once submitted, an application stays valid for twelve months and is considered for every residency scheduled in that period, after which an artist may reapply. Applications are reviewed by the BEERS London team and guest curators on quality, clarity of proposal and feasibility, up to five artworks may be uploaded, and shortlisted applicants are contacted by email. The application fee is £20, or £25 if applying concurrently to the gallery's open call group exhibition; the gallery states the fee covers administration, selection review, platform and processing costs and does not guarantee acceptance. Participation does not guarantee representation or sales, and a standard 50/50 commission applies to any work sold. The inaugural resident, announced for the spring 2026 session, was the painter Georgia Dymock, whose residency closed with a solo exhibition in July 2026. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: £20 (£25 with the group exhibition open call). Prize: Residency.

item.title: 2027 Meridian Scholar Program · University of Tampa
item.description: The University of Tampa's Department of Art + Design invites applications for the 2027 Meridian Scholar Program, a ten-day residency (formerly STUDIO-f) hosted on the university's downtown Tampa campus and open to artists, designers, creative practitioners and researchers. The 2027 cycle is built around the theme of Worldbuilding and seeks creative practitioners who intend to print, cast or digitally fabricate multiple editions during the residency period; photography is one of the accepted categories alongside craft, drawing, film/video/new media, mixed media, painting and sculpture. The selected resident works in the department's facilities in the Ferman Center for the Arts and the 30,000-square-foot R. K. Bailey Art Studios, which house drawing, printmaking, painting and ceramics studios, a photography laboratory and darkroom, and a Fab Lab equipped with laser cutters, 3D printers, CNC routers and vinyl cutters, and is given a working space alongside the department's advanced student studios. Residents are expected to involve UTampa studio art, graphic design, art therapy and museum studies students in the preparation, production and post-production of the project, to give a public lecture and Q&A, to engage with at least one class through a critique, workshop or demonstration, and to present work made during the residency in a public exhibition. The residency runs 15 to 26 March 2027. Past visiting artists include Sam Gilliam, Joyce J. Scott, Miriam Schapiro, Audrey Flack, Larry Poons and, in 2026, the Cuban artist Mabel Poblet Pujol. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Emergency Grants · Foundation for Contemporary Arts
item.description: Created in 1993, the Foundation for Contemporary Arts' Emergency Grants provide urgent, project-based funding to visual and performing artists and poets who have sudden, unanticipated opportunities to present their work to the public with insufficient time to seek other funding, or who incur unexpected or unbudgeted expenses for projects close to completion with committed exhibition dates. It is a year-round, multi-disciplinary programme open to artists living and working anywhere in the United States, for projects taking place in the US and abroad. FCA receives around 100 applications a month and makes roughly 15 to 20 grants of $500 to $3,000 each; applicants may request any amount in that range and the average grant is currently $2,200. The panel is made up of established practising artists from the disciplines FCA supports and meets monthly, weighing the urgency of the request, the significance of the opportunity, the impact the money would have and the strength of the work samples. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, and the foundation's mission is explicitly to support experimental and contemporary practice. Applicants must have a US Tax ID, must be individual artists rather than curators, producers or organisations, must have a confirmed presentation with specific dates at the time of applying, and must not be enrolled in any degree-granting programme. FCA asks that artists apply eight to ten weeks before the public presentation date. Grants may cover artist fees, airfare, accommodation, materials, shipping, fabrication and production; work-in-progress showings, projects presented by commercial galleries or art fairs, and any opportunity that requires the artist to pay to participate are not eligible. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$3,000.

item.title: Next Generation: University Art Competition 2026 · Honeywell Arts & Entertainment
item.description: Honeywell Arts & Entertainment runs Next Generation: University Art Competition, a free statewide juried exhibition for students currently enrolled at an accredited Indiana college or university and working towards an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree in any field of fine art or craft. Students on other degree paths are welcome to apply, and the jurors are asked to consider artistic quality and merit regardless of degree. Any two-dimensional or three-dimensional work is accepted provided it fits the gallery, and the presentation rules distinguish photographic and digital work from other media, so photographers may enter prints. Selected work goes on display from 10 December 2026 to 13 January 2027 in the Clark Gallery, which wraps the semicircular Porter Lobby of the Honeywell Center in Wabash and sees more than 170,000 visitors a year across 10-plus exhibits. Awards total $845 across seven cash prizes — $175 Best of Show, then $150, $100 and $85 for first, second and third place in each of the 2D and 3D categories — with six honourable mentions, all announced at the public closing reception on 13 January at 5:30pm. Work must be original, completed within three years of the deadline, not previously shown at the Clark Gallery, and no taller than 8.5 feet, deeper than 2 feet or wider than 5 feet; because the gallery is a public multi-use space, nudity and other adult content are not accepted. Entry is free through CaFE, which accepts up to three images. Honeywell Arts & Entertainment is part of The Honeywell Foundation, a nonprofit public charity that also programmes the Eagles Theatre, Charley Creek Gardens and five other venues in the Wabash cultural district. — Deadline: November 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $845 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 16th Annual International Juried Exhibition · Gallery 110
item.description: Gallery 110's annual juried exhibition, running since 2011, invites emerging and established artists worldwide to submit original work in any two- or three-dimensional medium — photography included — for a show in the gallery's Pioneer Square space from 4 to 27 February 2027. The 2026 juror is Ryan Hardesty, Executive Director of the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art at Washington State University, who spent twelve years at the Northwest Museum of Arts & Culture in Spokane and has held positions at the Institute of Contemporary Art in Boston, the Rose Art Museum at Brandeis and the Fogg Art Museum at Harvard. Hardesty has chosen an open call with no set theme. He awards first, second and third prizes of $1,000, $500 and $300, and there is a $200 People's Choice award. Gallery 110 is an artist-run 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by 4Culture and the City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture; accepted artists get professional reviews and inclusion in the monthly First Thursday Art Walk, which draws over a thousand visitors. Applications are accepted from 21 July to 31 October 2026. Finalists are notified by email and phone in December 2026 and are responsible for delivery and prepaid return shipping. Open to artists 18 and over. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $40 (3 images) + $10 each addl, up to 10. Prize: $1,000 / $500 / $300 + $200 People's Choice.

item.title: Call for Entries 2027 · ROY G BIV Gallery
item.description: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists in Columbus, Ohio runs its exhibition programme from one annual call for entries, and this is the round for the 2027 season. Selected artists are given a month-long small group exhibition during the 2027 calendar year, curated by the gallery director. Submissions come from artists local and global and are reviewed and voted on by a panel of jurors from the contemporary arts community; the 2027 jurors are filmmaker and visual artist Yusef Ferguson, a 2025 Greater Columbus Arts Council Visual Arts Fellow currently exhibiting at the Columbus Museum of Art, and sculptor Dana Lynn Harper, who holds an MFA from Penn State and makes ritual votive works about racial identity and cultural heritage. ROY defines emerging artists as those early in their careers, not represented by a gallery, and not yet substantially celebrated by the media, funding circles or the public; artists who have shown at ROY before are ineligible apart from ImageOHIO and the annual small works member show. Entry requires a ROY G BIV membership costing $25 for the calendar year. Submissions go by email with up to 10 images (JPG or PNG, under 1.5 MB each) or up to 5 video URLs, plus an artist statement, CV and list of works. Two-dimensional work must arrive ready to hang, and artists are responsible for transport and installation. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $25 membership. Prize: None listed.

item.title: RAA&M National Juried Show 2026 · Rockport Art Association & Museum
item.description: The Rockport Art Association & Museum's annual national juried exhibition hangs in the Aldro T. Hibbard and Maddocks galleries on Cape Ann from 14 November to 31 December 2026, with a gala and awards reception on 13 November. Photography is one of the named media categories, alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, collage, original printmaking and sculpture. Over $25,000 in cash and merchandise awards is on offer, including a $5,000 Grand Prize. Garin Baker is juror of selection and of awards. Artists may submit up to four works but only one will be selected if accepted; the maximum size is 36 inches on the longest side plus a reasonable frame. Membership is not required to enter. The museum takes a 40% commission on sales from the exhibition. Work made in an instructional setting, including workshops and classes, is not eligible, and accepted work must stay hanging until the show closes unless sold. The AI policy is unusually specific for a photography entrant: no artificial intelligence may be used in the conception or development of the work, images must originate with the artist through a light capture process, and no synthetic images, stock imagery, replacement skies or generative fill are permitted. Editing is allowed as long as every component belongs to the artist. Results appear in the OnlineJuriedShows artist profile on 25 September 2026. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $50 first entry ($40 members) + $10 each addl. Prize: $25,000+ in awards ($5,000 Grand Prize).

item.title: DeHaan Artist of Distinction Award 2026 — Round 2 · Indy Arts Council
item.description: Funded entirely by a legacy gift from the Christel DeHaan Family Foundation and administered by the Indy Arts Council, the DeHaan Artist of Distinction Award honours up to five contemporary visual artists a year with project grants of up to $10,000 each. Photography is named in the list of eligible art forms alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, textiles and digital or new media. The programme is built for risk: it funds aspirational, innovative projects that push an artist's practice in new directions, and applicants are asked to make the case that their work brings something new to the field. Applicants must have lived or worked in Indiana for at least three consecutive years at the date of application, must remain in the state for a year after the award activities conclude, must show five years of documented experience through solo exhibitions, national exposure, critical reviews, residencies, fellowships or juried shows, and must have generated consistent income from their work in visual art. Projects must conclude within twelve months of the signed agreement, and awardees take part in a professionally curated group exhibition at Gallery 924 at the Indy Arts Council and submit a final report documenting the project's impact. There are two rounds a year; Round 1 closed on 3 May 2026 and Round 2 closes on 18 October 2026. Applications are free and go through the council's grant platform, and alternative formats such as dictated or video responses can be arranged. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to 5 × $10,000.

item.title: 16th Annual National Juried Exhibition · Marshall University Art Galleries
item.description: Marshall University's School of Art & Design invites artists to its 16th Annual National Juried Exhibition, shown in the Charles W. and Norma C. Carroll Gallery in the Visual Arts Center in Huntington, West Virginia from 18 January to 25 February 2027, with an awards reception on 18 February. Artists may submit up to three works in any medium, so photography and lens-based work are eligible. The juror is Rachel Rearick, Executive Director of Contemporary Craft and an adjunct faculty member at Carnegie Mellon University teaching museum operations and public art; she is an artist member of the Associated Artists of Pittsburgh and the Pittsburgh Print Group. Entrants must be 18 or over and hold permanent residence in the United States, with exceptions for students and military personnel holding US resident status; work previously shown in a Marshall University gallery will not be considered. Entry is $30 for up to three works, or $15 for current Marshall students with ID, and everything is handled through the entry form on the gallery's own site. Jurying runs 3 to 14 November 2026 with email notifications on 18 November, and accepted work must reach the gallery between 7 and 11 December. All accepted pieces must arrive display-ready, and artists cover delivery and insurance in transit. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $30 (up to 3 entries; $15 Marshall students). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence — January–May 2027 · Surel's Place
item.description: A month-long live-work residency in Garden City, Idaho, in the house built by the late artist Surel Mitchell. The residency is free to apply to and free to hold: rent, utilities and wi-fi are covered, and residents receive a $100-per-week living stipend, a $300 travel stipend, use of the house bicycles, free or discounted tickets to local art events, marketing through the organisation's channels, and logistics and installation help for their public events. Each resident is assigned a host who introduces them to the local arts community. The programme is open to professional visual, literary and performance artists — the org describes it as "any artist who needs a place to focus" — though the property cannot accommodate loud or messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing, and work that is predominantly conceptual may find less enthusiasm with the jury. Residents must live at the house for the residency (no studio-only stays), take no other employment during it, give at least one public workshop of two to three hours, present a show or lecture on the residency work, and donate one piece to Surel's Place for future fundraising. The commission on sales arising from the residency is 35%. Applicants must be 25 or older and non-smokers; partners may join but children and pets cannot. This September 1 deadline covers residencies running January to May 2027; applications for playwrights and screenwriters are paused until the March 2027 round. Visual artists apply by email with a cover letter, a proposal including a workshop outline, a CV, and 4 to 6 images with an image list. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 1-month residency + stipends.

item.title: 1858 Prize for Contemporary Southern Art 2026 · Gibbes Museum of Art
item.description: An annual award from the Gibbes Museum of Art and its Society 1858 auxiliary, given to an artist whose work contributes to a new understanding of art in the South. The prize welcomes applications from artists working across any media, and photography has a long history here — past winners and finalists include Sally Mann, William Christenberry, Deborah Luster, Birney Imes, Stephen Marc, Jeff Whetstone, Susan Worsham, Jennifer Shaw and 2025 finalist Tommy Kha. Alongside the monetary award, a work chosen by the Gibbes curatorial team in collaboration with the artist goes on display in the museum's Mary Jackson Modern and Contemporary Galleries for the year following the announcement. Previous winners have gone on to Joan Mitchell Fellowships, Guggenheim Memorial Foundation awards and Pollock-Krasner grants, with work entering the collections of the National Gallery of Art, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Art Institute of Chicago. Eligibility is geographic rather than medium-based: artists must reside in, work in, or be from Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia or the District of Columbia. Applications go through SlideRoom with a registration form, an artist statement of 150 words or less, a CV, and a portfolio of up to ten images or videos of recent original work at 300dpi or better. Submissions are reviewed by a panel of visual arts professionals, Society 1858 representatives and Gibbes staff; the winner and finalists are notified in October 2026, with a public announcement later in the year. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Berlendis Venice Art Prize 2027 · Marignana Arte
item.description: The second edition of a Venice prize run by Kosmos Contemporary Venice APS with Marignana Arte, on the theme "Have We Crossed the Threshold? A Journey Beyond Borders, Identities and Languages" — crossing as an aesthetic, political and existential practice. Photography is explicitly named among the eligible media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking and graphic arts, collage, sculpture and installation, textile art and video art. A jury of eight selects twenty finalists, ten in an Emergent section for artists aged 18 to 30 and ten in a Contemporary section for artists over 30, who show together at Spazio Berlendis — a 300-square-metre former boatyard carpentry workshop in Cannaregio that has hosted the Gwangju Biennale and currently houses the Grenada and Guatemala pavilions of the 2026 Biennale Arte. The finalists' exhibition runs 20 February to 21 March 2027 with a dedicated publication, and every finalist receives a free copy. Cash prizes are €1,000 gross to the Emergent winner and €2,500 gross to the Contemporary winner, with withholding tax of 25% for Italian residents and 30% for others. Five further special prizes offer exhibitions: two solo shows at Marignana Project in 2027 (one per section), a group show at Fondazione THE BANK ETS in Bassano del Grappa, a solo or group show at Galleria Alessandro Casciaro in Bolzano or Venice, and a solo or group show at Spazio Magazzino. Each artist submits one work, up to 200×200cm for two-dimensional pieces and 20kg maximum, with a 4-to-10-page PDF portfolio and one to three images. Works remain the property of the artists, but shipping both ways, customs and insurance are at the artist's expense. Finalists are announced by 10 December 2026. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: €25 (18–30) / €35 (over 30). Prize: €2,500 + €1,000 + 5 exhibition prizes.

item.title: Foundwork Artist Prize 2026
item.description: An annual juried award recognising outstanding emerging and mid-career artists working in any media. The honoree receives an unrestricted $10,000 grant, a studio visit with each of the five jurors, and an interview for Foundwork's Dialogues programme; three further artists are named to a Short List and each receives a $1,000 micro-grant. The 2026 jury is Stefan Benchoam (artist and co-founder of Proyectos Ultravioleta and NuMu, Guatemala City), François Ghebaly (founder of the Los Angeles and New York gallery), Manuela Moscoso (director of the Center for Art, Research and Alliances and curator of Ecuador's 2026 Venice pavilion), Gabi Ngcobo (director of Kunstinstituut Melly, Rotterdam, and curator of the 10th Berlin Biennale) and Esther Schipper (founder of the Berlin gallery). Photography is well represented: the 2025 honoree Antonia Kuo works with photochemical painting on silver gelatin paper, and photographer Clifford Prince King was on the 2023 Short List. There is no separate entry fee, but applicants must hold an active Foundwork artist membership — $6 a month, with a 30-day free trial for new members — and keep a published profile carrying at least six artworks and an artist statement throughout the selection period, which runs from 5pm PT on 25 September 2026 to 5pm PT on 31 December 2026. Staff shortlist fifty finalists for the jury, who pick one honoree and three Short List artists. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over, except residents of Argentina, Arizona, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Cuba, Iran, Kosovo, Latvia, Macedonia, North Korea, Quebec, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Sudan, Syria and the UAE. Past honorees cannot win again, and past Short List artists must wait three years. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free (membership $6/month required). Prize: $10,000 + 3 × $1,000.

item.title: Hornsby Art Prize 2026 · Hornsby Shire Council
item.description: Established in 2009 and run by Hornsby Shire Council with the Hornsby Art Society, this non-acquisitive prize celebrates Australian contemporary art across five categories — Painting, Drawing, Printmaking, Photography and Sculpture — each carrying its own $1,500 award, so photographers compete for a dedicated Photography Award as well as the $10,000 major prize. The overall pool is $23,000, which also covers a $5,000 Hornsby Shire Local Artist Award and a $500 People's Choice. There is no set theme. Artists may enter up to two works; 2D pieces are capped at 125cm in height and width including the frame, and nothing may exceed 15kg. Finalist works must not have appeared in any other art prize exhibition and must be for sale, with a 20% commission going to the Hornsby Art Society. Finalists are announced by 5pm on 1 September and the exhibition runs at Wallarobba Arts and Cultural Centre from 16 October to 1 November 2026, with the prize announced on opening day. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: AU$40 per entry. Prize: AU$10,000 + AU$1,500 Photography Award.

item.title: Kangaroo Valley Art Prize 2026 · Visual Arts in the Valley
item.description: The headline prize of the Visual Arts in the Valley festival, held in the Kangaroo Valley Hall and venues around the valley in the NSW Southern Highlands. The terms of entry are deliberately wide: any original work of visual art by an Australian artist or an artist residing in Australia is eligible, expressly including photographic art, digital art, new media and video alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, textiles and collage. Work must have been made within two years of the closing date and must not have been shown by Visual Arts in the Valley before; maximum hung size is 115cm wide by 180cm high including the frame. Alongside the $10,000 main prize there is a $3,000 Highly Commended, a $2,000 Commended, a $4,000 Young & Emerging Art Prize for artists aged 30 or under (with a $1,000 Commended), a $1,500 Salon of Local Artists Prize, a $1,000 People's Choice and a $500 Packing Room Prize. Judged by painter Steven Harvey, senior lecturer at the National Art School, with Olivia Welch of Ngununggula Regional Gallery curating. The exhibition runs 2–5 October 2026. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: AU$30 per work (AU$80 for three). Prize: AU$10,000 + AU$4,000 Young & Emerging.

item.title: The Ingram Prize 2026 · The Ingram Collection
item.description: An annual purchase prize for artists within five years of graduating from a UK-based art school, run by The Ingram Collection — one of the largest publicly accessible collections of modern and contemporary British art. Entry is free, any medium is accepted, there is no size restriction, and artists may submit up to two works. Three artists receive the Ingram Prize and have their work acquired for the Collection; a fourth work is chosen personally by founder Chris Ingram for the Founder's Award; and one prizewinner is given a solo exhibition at Lightbox Gallery, Woking, in 2027. Shortlisted work is shown at Unit 1 Gallery | Workshop in London from 5 to 11 November 2026, with the winners announced at the opening event on 4 November. Eligible applicants are those aged 18 or over holding a practice-based visual arts qualification from a UK institution completed between 1 April 2021 and 31 October 2026. — Deadline: August 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Acquisition + solo exhibition.

item.title: Heysen Prize for Landscape 2026 · Hahndorf Academy
item.description: A biennial contemporary art prize established in 1997 to commemorate Sir Hans Heysen, run by the Hahndorf Academy in the Adelaide Hills. The 2026 edition asks artists to express their connection with — or concern for — protecting the Australian environment, taking Heysen's own record as an early environmental activist as its starting point. 'Landscape' is defined broadly to include every aspect of the natural, rural and urban landscape, and the prize is open to 2D, 3D and moving-image work; photographers have been regular finalists, and past selections include Che Chorley and Mark Kimber. The main prize of $15,000 is acquisitive; a non-acquisitive People's Choice Prize of $1,000 is also awarded. Finalists are notified on 31 August 2026 and deliver work to Hahndorf between 7 and 23 September; the finalist exhibition runs 10 October to 6 December 2026, opening with a launch on 10 October at which the winners are announced. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: AU$55. Prize: AU$15,000 acquisitive.

item.title: Windgate Artist in Residence — Fall 2027 & Spring 2028 · UA Little Rock School of Art and Design
item.description: A semester-long funded residency at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, supported by the Windgate Foundation and open to artists, designers and craftspeople in any medium. The selected artist receives a $30,000 stipend for the semester, housing, a $2,000 materials and travel budget, and 24-hour access to a private studio plus the Windgate Center's specialist facilities — a photography studio, printmaking studio, woodshop with CNC and laser cutter, ceramics, jewellery and metalsmithing studios, and a smithy and foundry. Residents are not required to teach courses; the commitments are weekly open studio hours, two public artist talks (one at the Windgate Center, one at the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts), one two-day student workshop, BFA critiques and up to two guest class sessions, plus donating one work to the university's permanent collection. Two terms are open: Fall 2027 (15 August to 15 December) and Spring 2028 (15 January to 15 May), each with its own application. Applicants need an active practice, evidence of exhibiting nationally or internationally, experience working with students, and a degree, certificate or equivalent experience; international artists must already hold visa authorisation covering the residency, as the university cannot sponsor visas. Applications go through Workday with a cover letter, CV, three references and a portfolio of up to 20 images. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30,000 stipend + housing.

item.title: Create! Magazine Issue #60 — The Artist's World
item.description: Open call for Issue No. 60 of Create! Magazine, an artist-led print and digital publication for contemporary art. The theme, The Artist's World, asks what it means to build a world as an artist — a universe made through the work, an independent practice that makes its own opportunities, or simply inhabiting the planet; the brief is open to all interpretations and all subjects and media are welcome, photography among them. Juried by Marina Granger, founder of the New York advisory The Artist Advisory, former guest curator of the magazine's 2024 Women's Print Issue and curator of Lunation at Warnes Contemporary and The Feminine Divine at Kaliner Gallery. Selected artists receive a four-page spread in the print and digital editions, website and social features, and a complimentary digital issue. Submit up to 10 works (cohesive bodies and series encouraged) with a 300-word bio and artist statement; $35 covers three images. Open to artists worldwide with no academic background required, and there are no further fees if published. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: Publication.

item.title: XIV «Galicia» Award of Contemporary Photography · Outono Fotográfico
item.description: The fourteenth edition of the Premio «Galicia» de Fotografía Contemporánea, founded in 2013 within the International Outono Fotográfico Festival and run by the Asociación OF. Outono Fotográfico with the Xunta de Galicia, the Deputación de Lugo and the University of Vigo's Ourense campus. It seeks complete photographic projects on a free theme, judged above all on how they sit within the discourse of contemporary photography, and is open to any author working with photography or the photographic regardless of nationality. Two awards are made from the same pool of entries. The Jury Prize produces an exhibition of the winning project with a curator appointed by the association, opening in Lugo and touring Galicia and Portugal for two years before the exhibition becomes the artist's property, plus a book in the "Galicia Contemporary Photography Prize" series from Difusora de Letras, Artes e Ideas, distributed in bookshops with a percentage of the print run to the author. The Organisation Prize produces a comparable exhibition at the Alterarte Gallery on the Ourense campus with an accompanying booklet. Projects must have been made between October 2016 and October 2026 and must not have been fully funded by another competition or published in full. Submit up to 15 images (minimum 3,000 px on the long side) with a synopsis of up to 2,500 characters and a 1,500-character biography. Entry costs €22 per project. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: €22 per project. Prize: Touring exhibition + book.

item.title: Nocturne: Photography After Dark · TCG Gallery
item.description: International juried online exhibition on the night — what becomes visible once daylight recedes and darkness, limited visibility and artificial light reshape the world. Streetlights isolating gestures, windows glowing against dark buildings, long exposures stretching time, flash revealing what the eye would miss; beyond the city, moonlight, stars, weather and deep shadow remaking the landscape. Urban night photography, nocturnal landscapes, astrophotography, nightlife, interiors, staged scenes, low-light portraits, light painting and experimental work are all welcome, with night read as a physical setting, a psychological condition or simply a space where ordinary life behaves differently. Digital, film, alternative process, documentary, fine art, conceptual and mixed-media photographic work accepted. Blind review wherever possible, with emphasis on the work rather than biography or exhibition history; approximately 30 images are selected for the curated online exhibition and permanent website archive, running 1–21 November 2026. Fee waivers are offered on the honour system for artists experiencing financial hardship. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Environmental Wildlife
item.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of environmental wildlife — animals shown in the context of the landscape they live in — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 333) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a Cumulus Moonrain Jacket (RRP £325). Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). Free to enter, uploaded in bulk through the magazine's Google Form. The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres, and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cumulus Moonrain Jacket (£325) + Publication.

item.title: SELF PORTRAIT Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery invites photographers worldwide to submit their best self portrait work for a themed gallery show in Tucson, Arizona. The gallery frames self portraiture as an exploration of identity and an intimate glimpse into the life of the artist, and is looking for work that reveals a story rather than simply records a likeness. At least twenty-six images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode Gallery after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper, and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats in a range of sizes. Submitted files are never cropped, only scaled for the best fit in the mat. One print is made per accepted image and archived in a flat file for two years after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs, open to amateurs and professionals alike. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due two days later. The exhibition runs November 7 to 28, 2026, opening on November 7. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with the gallery taking a 50 per cent commission and all rights to the file and print remaining with the photographer. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: HUMOROUS: The Art of Laughter · Armory Art Center
item.description: The Armory Art Center's juried gallery exhibition for Florida-based artists, hung alongside the tenth annual Creative Market on its historic West Palm Beach campus in Howard Park. The theme is humour in all its registers: playful portraiture and caricature, visual puns and wordplay, absurd and surreal scenes, comics and graphic narratives, everyday life with a twist, pop-culture and nostalgia parody, and animal antics. The Armory argues that humour in art does more than amuse, that it shifts perspectives, crosses language and cultural lines, and gives satire a way to critique politics and social norms. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside oil, acrylic, water media, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fibre, wood, ceramics and digital art; AI-generated work is not accepted, and diptychs and triptychs must be uploaded as a single image. Entry is $43 plus processing for up to two pieces, each judged individually, so the jury may take neither, one or both. The show is curated and juried by Armory staff with an anonymous juror, and first, second and third awards are given. Open to amateur and professional artists eighteen and over living in Florida. Notification is by October 16 and the exhibition runs November 2 to December 26, 2026 with a reception on November 19. All work must be for sale, with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and artists cover shipping both ways. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $43 (up to 2 works). Prize: Awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Exhibition Proposals · Falkirk Cultural Center
item.description: The City of San Rafael invites artists, groups and organisations to propose exhibitions for the 2027 calendar at two civic venues: Falkirk Cultural Center, an 1888 Queen Anne mansion on the National Historic Register whose three second-floor rooms have shown art since the City took it on in 1974, and the recently renovated San Rafael Downtown Library, one of California's Carnegie libraries, open again after a restoration that preserved the 1909 building. Falkirk hosts five or six exhibits a year, each running roughly six weeks, with most openings timed to the Downtown San Rafael Second Friday Art Walk. Proposals are judged on community interest, quality of work and a track record of achievement, and applicants are asked to show they can curate an exhibit large enough to fill one gallery room at Falkirk or the Library's display shelves, which are built for three-dimensional work. There is no medium restriction and no residency requirement stated. Proposals go first to City staff, then to the Public Art Review Board in October, and selected proposals move into a contract. Exhibitors handle their own transport, installation, take-down, title cards and opening reception, and provide images good enough for the City to build a virtual version of the show for accessibility; the City provides staffing during open hours, show cards and promotion. Sales run through the City on a 70/30 split in the artist's favour. Application is $5 through CaFE. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.
